summary: G. Gordon Liddy, an FBI agent and prosecutor obsessed with Nazi-style willpower, ran Nixon's dirty-tricks unit and the 1972 Watergate break-in, then served prison time and became a far-right talk radio host.

evidence.note: German housekeeper shares Nazi radio broadcasts with young Liddy, seeding his lifelong fascist admiration
detailed account of him roasting and eating a dead rat, later killing a squirrel and chickens
as Dutchess County prosecutor he joins the raid on Timothy Leary's Millbrook mansion
Treasury post: helps organize Operation Intercept against drug smuggling at the Mexican border
1971: joins the White House Plumbers after the Pentagon Papers leak, start of main span
Liddy and Hunt send their team into the DNC offices at the Watergate in 1972
habitually burns his own hand and arm to build pain tolerance
in prison he deliberately starves himself, framed by the host as self-harm
released in 1977 after 52 months once Carter commutes his sentence, end of main span
early 1990s launch of his syndicated talk radio show and its inflammatory content
acting roles such as Miami Vice, later a Fear Factor celebrity episode
dies in spring 2021 aged 90, end of covered span

notes: Primary theme could arguably be fascism-far-right (title framing); chose electoral-politics because the core is Nixon-campaign dirty tricks and Watergate. Long Waffen SS myth-busting digression in part 3 is commentary, so nazism was left out. Ian Johnson sits in as editor in parts 5-6 and is not listed as a guest. Brief Mexican border segment did not justify MX in setting.
